title: Appeals and Grievances Intake Rule: One Case per Decision and Case Type
content:
**Appeals and Grievances** cases are combined per decision: one decision or concern is handled in one case per case type.

## Rule

A new case is not opened when the member already has a case of the same case type for the same related reference in filed, acknowledged or under review status. New information about an open case is added to it as evidence instead.

The limit is the most open cases of one case type for the same related reference that the case type allows, which the case types' terms set at one. The related reference is the decision or trip reference the case is about.

## Basis of the check

- **Authority.** The check rests on the member's existing case records held by the plan, not on the member's account of what is open. It is made before a new case is opened.
- **What is compared.** Three things must all match an existing case: the same member, the same related reference and the same case type.
- **Which cases count.** Only cases whose status is filed, acknowledged or under review count, taken as they stand on the day the request is handled. A resolved or withdrawn case does not count.

## Decision table

| Existing case of the same member with the same related reference | Same case type | Status of that case | New case of that type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Filed, acknowledged or under review | Not opened; the new information is added to the open case as evidence |
| Yes | Yes | Resolved or withdrawn | Not barred by this rule |
| Yes | No | Any | Not barred by this rule |
| No | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not barred by this rule |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A member has a Standard Appeal under review about a prior authorization denial with a given decision reference, and calls with a new letter from the treating provider about that same denial. No second Standard Appeal is opened for that reference; the letter is added to the open Standard Appeal as evidence.
2. A member's Member Grievance about a given trip reference was withdrawn. A new Member Grievance about the same trip reference is not barred by this rule, since the earlier case is no longer filed, acknowledged or under review.
3. A member has an acknowledged Standard Appeal about one claim denial and asks to appeal a different claim denial with its own claim reference. The related references differ, so this rule does not bar a Standard Appeal for the second claim.
